findings.problem: The scene reads as a vertical list of six equations (prime p, prime q, n = 5 x 11 = 55, z = (5 - 1) x (11 - 1) = 40, e = 3 plus a tick, d = 27 plus a check line): the 'could be replaced by a bullet list' failure. The one picture meant to show where n and z come from (a 5 x 11 cell grid whose inner 4 x 10 block is z) is tiny (about 230 x 100 px, 18 px cells) and carries no labels for 5, 11, 4 or 10, nor anything saying what the purple block means. The padlock and key pictograms, which are the point of the scene (public key = lock, private key = key), only arrive at about 9.9 s, so for the first 9 s the right-hand 40% of the stage is empty and the scene is left-heavy.
findings.fix: Make the grid the hero: cells at least 24 px, a '5' label down its left side and an '11' label across its top (28 px or more, blue = public), and when z lands label the purple inner block '4' and '10' and fade the dashed last row and column so the subtraction is seen as removing a row and a column. Bring the pictograms in as the numbers are chosen, not at the end: when n and e are published a blue padlock slides in beside them ('public'), when d is found a purple key appears beside it ('secret'), so the closing caption only confirms what is already on screen. Keep the arithmetic tags but treat them as labels on the picture.
findings.evidence: s5@3.4 and s5@4.6 (tiny unlabelled grid, empty right half), s5@8.0 (still no lock or key), s5@9.8 and s5@11.5 (lock and key only now); scene-05-rsa-keys.js CELL = {size: 18, gap: 3}.

findings.problem: Caption 'Recompute every later hash and it looks valid again.' (8.2-10.8) runs ahead of its picture and is contradicted by it. The chain only looks valid when the badge flips at about 10.75 s; for the first 2.5 s of the caption the stage shows a red cross on link 2-3, a red block 3 and the badge 'broken chain'. It also never says who recomputes the hashes: the forger (Eve) is not on screen, so a first-time learner does not know whose action this is.
findings.fix: Describe the action while it happens and put the payoff in the next caption: [8.2, 10.4, 'A forger recomputes each later hash to repair every link.'] then [10.8, 12.4, 'Now it looks valid again. Hashes spot edits, they do not stop them.'] (merge or drop the 11.0 caption; the badge 'valid chain' and the tag 'but the edit is still there' carry the point).
findings.evidence: s8@8.4 and s8@9.6 (caption 'looks valid again' over red cross and 'broken chain'), s8@10.7 (all ticks but badge still 'broken chain'), s8@12.0 (badge finally 'valid chain'); caps at scene-08-chain.js line 359.

findings.problem: Caption 'Each extra zero makes a hit 16 times rarer.' (8.8-11.0) runs ahead of its picture. For the whole caption the stage shows only a 16-square strip with 'starts with 0: 1 in 16'; the second zero ('starts with 00: 1 in 256', T.tag256 = 10.6) and the '16 times more work' sticker (T.work = 11.3) arrive when the caption has all but ended. At 8.8-9.4 the stage is nearly blank (a grey label and a 6-square strip), because part 1 fades out at 8.4-8.8 before part 2 has started.
findings.fix: Re-time the captions to the picture: [8.8, 10.9, 'One hash in 16 starts with 0.'] then [11.1, 13.3, 'Add a second zero: 1 in 256, so 16 times more work.'] (replacing the current 8.8 and 11.2 captions), or bring tag256, the 256-cell square and the work sticker forward to about 9.8-10.2. Let part 1 hold until the strip starts growing so there is no blank beat.
findings.evidence: s9@9.2 (caption 'Each extra zero...' over an empty stage and a 6-square strip), s9@10.4 (still only '1 in 16'), s9@11.6 (1 in 256 and '16 times more work' arrive); caps at scene-09-mining.js line 256, T at lines 95-112.

findings.problem: The 1-in-16 and 1-in-256 pictures are misleading. The 16 x 16 square has exactly one lit square (the same square as in the first strip) and nothing else, so it reads as 'one hash in 256 starts with 0'. If one hash in 16 starts with 0, about one square in every row should be lit, and only one of those would also start with 00. A learner who looks at the grid cannot see why the second zero makes the hit '16 times rarer': the 'rarer' ratio is only in the labels.
findings.fix: Colour the squares from the real hashes (assert the counts in the helper): pale green for 'starts with 0' (about 16 squares, roughly one per row) and one solid green square, ringed, for 'starts with 00'. Then the strip is 1 in 16, the whole square is 1 in 256, and 'x 16' is visible as 16 pale hits per one solid hit.
findings.evidence: s9@10.4 and s9@11.6 (256 squares, one lit); scene-09-mining.js line 207 grid.update((r, c) => (r === 0 && c === HIT ? { tone: 'green' } : undefined)).

findings.problem: The scene's payoff (that rewriting history costs real work) is not on screen. The finished frame is three green ticks and a '50 tries' tag, which reads as a forgery that succeeded quickly; nothing shows what the original sealing cost or how big 50 is. The caption 'redoing all that work' points at work that is never drawn (scene 10 never shows the first hunts, only the finished nonces 27 / 24 / 16). Note that comparing with the original would not help: the original seals took 28 + 25 + 17 = 70 tries, so the redo (15 + 5 + 30 = 50) is a lucky cheaper one.
findings.fix: Show the work as a repeat of the hunt from scene 9: when each block is first sealed (at the start) let a small orange bar grow under it with its tries (28, 25, 17), then redo those same bars in grey-outline plus orange after the edit, labelled 'again'. End on a scale cue instead of a comparison: a purple or orange tag 'each extra zero: 16 times more work' (the scene 9 rule), so a toy 50 reads as small beside a real chain. Check the wording against lesson 8.7 before adding anything about real chains.
findings.evidence: s10@1.6 (sealed, no work shown), s10@9.4 and s10@10.8 (all green, '50 tries', no scale); facts: nonces 27/24/16 give 28+25+17 = 70 tries, re-mined 15+5+30 = 50.

findings.problem: The headline promises 'the same trick with numbers' but the mapping is never drawn. Nothing shows that g = 5 plays the public gold paint, a and b the rose and blue secrets, or that A = 5^6 mod 23 is 'public paint plus my secret'. The rule for the second half of the exchange ('raise what you received to your own secret') is never said either: at 8.0 the pills 19^6 mod 23 and 8^15 mod 23 just appear and the caption only reports the result. A learner who followed the paint scene cannot see which number is the mixture and which is the second drop. Also, the 5^6 = 15625 = 679 x 23 + 8 working appears centred between the two people, so it is unclear whose calculation it is.
findings.fix: Carry the paint colours across as small dots: a gold dot on the g tag, a rose dot on a = 6 and a blue dot on b = 15, and give A = 8 and B = 19 the orange and green mixture dots from scene 3. Say the rule in the caption at 8.0 ('Each raises what they received to their own secret: both get 2.'), and slide the 5^6 working out of Alice's secret a = 6 so it clearly belongs to her.
findings.evidence: s4@1.6 (p, g, a, b tags with no link to the paint), s4@3.0 and s4@4.6 (working floats mid-stage), s4@6.1 (A = 8 and B = 19 plain blue pills), s4@8.5 (19^6 and 8^15 with no stated rule).

findings.problem: The story never closes the loop to scene 2. The shared colour (scene 3) and the shared number 2 (scene 4) are never called the key. Scene 2 ends on 'how does Bob get the key without Eve seeing it?', yet scene 3 says 'the very same colour' and scene 4 says 'Both get 2', so a first-time learner may not realise this value IS the cipher key (the 5 in 'key 5') or why they wanted it.
findings.fix: Make the payoff the answer to the question: scene 4 caption 8.0-9.9 'Both get 2: a shared key that was never sent.' with a purple key icon and a '2' tag beside the green equals sign at about 9.3; scene 3: a key icon beside the green equals disc and caption 'the very same colour: their shared key.'
findings.evidence: s2@9.0 ('key 5 ... how does Bob get the key'), s3@9.8 (tan = tan, no key), s4@9.9 ('= 2', no key).

findings.problem: Eve's hunt hits x = 6 (green tile, '6 tries') but her dashed purple 'a = ?' tag never resolves, so the toy break has no visible consequence. A first-time learner cannot tell whether the 6-try search worked or failed, which weakens the contrast with the 617-digit number. Green (agreed / valid) is also the colour of her success, with nothing saying the toy exchange is broken.
findings.fix: When x = 6 turns green (about 12.8-13.2) turn the ghost 'a = ?' into a solid red 'a = 6' with a small pop, so the toy secret visibly leaks. Then '6 tries', the 617-digit number and the red 'no computer can search that' read as a clear before and after. Optionally recolour the hit tile red-on-light (Eve's colour).
findings.evidence: s4@12.9 and s4@14.5 (x = 6 green, 'a = ?' still dashed purple and unresolved).

findings.problem: The cipher step is not explained by the picture. The caption 'A cipher scrambles it with a secret key.' plays over six orange '+5' tags and tiles that flip edge-on in 0.35 s each; nothing says '+5' means 'move each letter 5 along the alphabet' or that the key IS the 5, and the viewer never sees S and X side by side (the tile is edge-on when it changes). A first-timer sees letters change and a number next to a key, not the rule.
findings.fix: Change the caption to say it ('A cipher shifts each letter 5 along. The key is 5.') and hold one finished pair for a beat (for example the first tile stays as S above X with a small arrow and '+5' for about 0.6 s before the rest flip). Optionally add a tiny grey 'toy cipher' tag beside the row.
findings.evidence: s2@5.2 and s2@5.6 (tiles mid-flip, one edge-on, +5 tags already on screen), s2@6.0 (XJHWJY, the original S E C R E T gone).

findings.problem: The core security claim 'Eve cannot unmix paint to find a secret.' (10.1-11.8) is drawn only as a small red question mark between her two copies, which pops at about 10.1-10.6 before the scene fades. The key idea (mixing is easy, unmixing is not) is asserted by the caption, not shown, and a learner can ask why Eve cannot simply add paint to what she holds. Scene 7 gives the same idea a proper picture (arrow with a red cross, 'no way back').
findings.fix: Draw one attempt: from Eve's orange copy a red arrow back toward the loose drops (gold, rose) ending in a red cross, or let her try to add a blue drop and get a brown that does not match the tan (red cross on the mismatch). Keep the '?' as the end state and hold it longer; it currently has under 1.5 s before the fade.
findings.evidence: s3@10.3 (just a '?' between the copies) and s3@11.8 (fading).

findings.problem: Two steps rely on jargon or magic the learner has not met. 'e = 3: it shares no factor with 40' ticks a green check with no demonstration, and 'factor' is only taught later (scene 6, 55 = 5 x 11). z = (5 - 1) x (11 - 1) appears as a formula with no reason for the subtraction. The learner cannot tell why e must be checked or why z must stay secret (only Bob knows 5 and 11).
findings.fix: Keep it visual: under 'e = 3' show the two factor lists (3: 1, 3 and 40: 1, 2, 4, 5, 8, 10, 20, 40) with only the 1 in common ringed in green, or reword the caption to 'Pick e = 3: only 1 divides both 3 and 40.' At the z step add a small purple lock label 'only Bob can work this out'. Folds into the grid fix above.
findings.evidence: s5@4.6 (z pill, no reason), s5@6.2 (green 'shares no factor with 40' and a tick, nothing shown).

findings.problem: Eve's attack skips the step that makes it work. The row reads '55 = 5 x 11' then 'so d = 27' with no z = 40 between them, so a learner who just watched scene 5 build d from z cannot see how knowing the factors gives the private key. The lower third is also the most crowded part of the video: nine pills (Eve's copies of the public key and 13, four trial divisions, '55 = 5 x 11', 'so d = 27', 'a real n: 617 digits') on two rows, plus the full lock and unlock arithmetic above them.
findings.fix: Insert a short pill between the two, 'z = 4 x 10 = 40', so the chain is factors, z, d (the three can share the second row; the '617 digits' tag can move to the free right-hand area or appear after the row fades). Keep all labels at 28 px or more.
findings.evidence: s6@10.4 (nine pills in the lower third; '55 = 5 x 11' then 'so d = 27').

findings.problem: The scene's conclusion is implicit and rushed. The headline says 'only Bob can unlock', but Eve's copies of 13 and (55, 3) just sit there with no attempt to unlock and no sign she cannot, and the scene then shows her successfully deriving d = 27 (the private-key card turns red). The closing 'A real n has 617 digits.' (10.4-12.0) is a blue pill with no consequence drawn, while scene 4's equivalent beat shows a red 'no computer can search that'. The learner must infer 'so factoring a real n is hopeless'; the beat gets under 1.7 s and the scene fades right after, so the last thing seen is RSA broken.
findings.fix: Make the caption carry the conclusion ('A real n has 617 digits: nobody can factor that.') and add the 'no computer can search that' style red cross or pill beside the 617-digit tag; consider turning the private-key card back to purple at the end. If the beat needs room, trim the 13^27 line's hold or start the Eve beat 0.5 s earlier.
findings.evidence: s6@5.0 and s6@6.6 (Eve holds 13 and (55, 3), no attempt shown), s6@10.4 (private key turns red, 'so d = 27'), s6@12.0 (final frame, only a blue '617 digits').

findings.problem: For about 1.3 s (about 4.4-5.7 s) the screen contradicts itself. Block 1 already shows the edited data and the new hash 9a1f8189, but the check row still reads 'hash of block 1: fb28ccb9' (the OLD value, green digits), the link tick is green and the badge says 'valid chain', while the caption says 'Edit one block and its hash changes.' A first-time learner may read 'valid chain' as the result of the edit.
findings.fix: Reset the check row and badge when the edit starts: grey the row and swap the badge to a neutral 'checking...' at the moment the block's data changes, then roll the new hash 9a1f8189 into the 'hash of block 1' slot just before the red cross at about 5.7, so the comparison always matches what the block shows.
findings.evidence: s8@4.8 (block 1 hash 9a1f8189 but check row fb28ccb9 = fb28ccb9, green ticks, 'valid chain').

findings.problem: The scene is top-heavy for most of its first half. Block 7 and the nonce list occupy only stage y 20-330; the lower half of the stage is empty from 0.5 to about 7 s (the 'find / check' bars arrive at 7 s). The nonce list clips rows at its top and bottom edge (half-visible 'nonce 2' / 'nonce 7'), which looks like overflow rather than a scroll window. The figure is small for a video that is about watching hashes fail.
findings.fix: Centre or enlarge the mining figure: move block 7, its tag and the nonce list down about 100 px, or make the rows taller (84 px) with a larger digest font so the figure fills stage y 40-420, then keep the bars below. Soften the list edges with a fade so the clipped rows read as scrolling.
findings.evidence: s9@1.8, s9@3.4, s9@5.0 and s9@6.4 (everything above y 600, lower 40% empty; half rows clipped at the dashed frame).

findings.problem: The three block cards sit flush against both stage edges (x 0-270, 333-603, 666-936; BLK = {y: 10, w: 270, step: 333}), so the house 12 px stage margin is broken (measured: left and right margin 0) and the cards jump when scene 8 hands over to scene 10 (scene 8's cards sit at x 12-924). Block 1's border and Block 3's lip touch the stage boundary.
findings.fix: Use x0 = 12 and step = 321 (cards stay 270 wide, gaps 51 px, right edge 924) and check that the link elbows and tick discs still fit the 51 px gaps; match scene 8's x positions so the handover looks continuous.
findings.evidence: s10@1.6 (cards flush with the page margin), measured with a bounding-box audit: scene 8 left/right margin 12/12, scene 10 0/0.

findings.problem: Recap card 3 says 'Hashes link blocks, edits cost real work' but its pictogram only shows blocks 1-2-3 linked, block 3 flashing red and turning green (a chain repaired). 'Edits cost real work' has nothing on screen: no mining bar, no tries, no 0 seal. Proof of work is the last third of the video and the recap drops it.
findings.fix: Finish the pictogram with the work idea: after the three blocks go green add a short orange bar (or a '50 tries' chip) under them, or give each block a small '0' seal chip. The pictogram should still play once and hold (it does today), and the final frame should stay calm.
findings.evidence: s11@6.0 and s11@8.9 (row 3: green 1-2-3 and ticks only).

findings.problem: 'Blockchain' is in the title card but never named again: scenes 8-10 are labelled 'HASH CHAIN' and 'PROOF OF WORK' and the recap says 'blocks'. The shift from secrets (scenes 2-6, Eve and the open wire) to trust (scenes 7-10, no Eve) is also silent: scene 7 simply opens with the kicker 'HASH', so a first-time learner does not know why a fingerprint appears after RSA, or that the second half answers a different question (how do we trust data?).
findings.fix: Name it where it first appears: scene 8 kicker 'BLOCKCHAIN: HASH CHAIN' (or add 'a blockchain' to the first caption) and recap card 3 'Chained hashes make a blockchain, edits cost real work'. Bridge in scene 7 with kicker 'TRUST: HASH' and one early caption 'Next question: how do we know data was not changed?'
findings.evidence: s7@1.8 (kicker 'HASH'), s8@1.6 (kicker 'HASH CHAIN'), s11@8.9 (no 'blockchain'); grep -i blockchain videos/a8/scene-*.js hits only comments and the title card.

findings.problem: Caption 'Checking takes just 1.' (7.3-8.4) has no unit, so it reads as an unfinished sentence; the bar beside it says 'check: 1 hash'.
findings.fix: Use 'Checking takes just 1 hash.' (M.checkCost is 1; build the caption from the same `check: ${M.checkCost} hash` string).
findings.evidence: s9@7.8 (caption 'Checking takes just 1.' above the 'check: 1 hash' bar).

findings.problem: Caption 'Change one letter and every digit changes.' (5.7-7.5) starts before its evidence: 'cot' appears at about 5.9 s, its fingerprint is typed out only at about 6.5-7.2 s, and the tag 'all 8 digits differ' lands at about 7.3 s, so the claim leads the picture by about 1.3 s.
findings.fix: Start the caption at about 6.4 (end 8.0) or reveal the cot fingerprint faster.
findings.evidence: s7@6.4 and s7@6.8 (fingerprint typed 'cb26'), s7@7.5 (complete, 'all 8 digits differ').

findings.problem: The headline breaks as 'A hash is a / fingerprint of data', leaving the article hanging at the end of line 1.
findings.fix: Use ['A hash is a fingerprint', 'of your data'] or ['A hash is', 'a fingerprint of data'].

findings.problem: Caption 'Edit block 1: its seal and the link both break.' (2.3-3.9) starts while the edit is still being typed ('ann pays EV' at 2.4 s) and the seal and link only break at about 3.0-3.4 s, so the caption leads its picture by about 0.7 s.
findings.fix: Start the caption at 2.8 (or 3.0) and end at 4.0.
findings.evidence: s10@2.4 (caption greyed, edit half typed, ticks intact), s10@3.9 (seal and link broken).

findings.problem: A dead beat at the hand-over between Alice and Bob's exchange and Eve's attack: from about 10.2 to 11.0 s the stage is almost empty (Eve and four tags along the top) and there is no caption, so the pacing stalls for nearly a second.
findings.fix: Start Eve's attack 0.4 s earlier, or let the equal sign and the two '= 2' pills hold until the tags have arrived.
findings.evidence: s4@10.6 and s4@10.9 (only Eve, four tags and the formula; caption gap 9.9-11.0).

findings.problem: Locking and unlocking are written differently: the lock card says '7^3 = 343 = 6 x 55 + 13' (no 'mod') while the unlock says '13^27 mod 55 = 7'. Scene 4 taught 'mod' as the remainder, so the first card should use the same words.
findings.fix: Add the tag '7^3 mod 55 = 13' (or the line 'mod 55 keeps the remainder') above the working, as scene 4 does.
findings.evidence: s6@5.0 (lock working without mod) versus s6@6.6 (unlock with mod).

findings.problem: Eve's red 'copy' arrow at 7.5-8.5 s starts at the wire's centre (x 468) but the blue row has slid to Bob's end (tile centres 522-842), so the arrow does not come from the letters it copies (in the first beat it did).
findings.fix: Start the arrow under the row (x about 680) and end it at Eve's copy row, or shift Eve's copy row to sit under it.

findings.problem: The video's red means Eve and broken, but Alice's literal secret paint is a saturated red (rose) that sits in a purple frame beside Eve's red-framed copies. It is a documented exception, yet at a glance the red pot at Alice's side can read as Eve's.
findings.fix: Shift the rose paint toward pink (more white-ish) or a purple-leaning magenta so the only saturated red on stage is Eve's.
findings.evidence: s3@7.0 and s3@11.1 (red pot on the left beside Eve's red-dashed copies).
